235	 * listener and falls under the unknown-code rule above.)
236	 */
237	type DbErrorCode =
238	  | "invalid_argument"
239	  | "resource_exhausted"
240	  | "quota_exceeded"
241	  | "unavailable"
242	  | "revoked"
243	  | "not_granted"
244	  | "capability_disabled"
245	  | "capability_removed"
246	  | "transform_error";
247	
248	/**
249	 * PATH GRAMMAR (shared by every ref). A document path has an EVEN
250	 * number of slash-separated segments — the last is the document id,
251	 * the joined rest is its collection (`tasks/t1`, or nested:
252	 * `boards/b1/columns/c2`). A collection path is the odd-length
253	 * prefix form (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`). Count segments before
254	 * choosing the builder. `data/users/<id>` (3) is a COLLECTION — the
255	 * viewer's own — so one document per viewer is
256	 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile")` (4), and one document per
257	 * deck is `db.collection("data/users/" + uid).doc(deckId)` (4).
258	 * `data/users/<id>/decks` (4) is therefore a DOCUMENT path, not a
259	 * collection: a named per-viewer list is a subcollection under a
260	 * per-viewer document,
261	 * `db.doc("data/users/" + uid + "/profile").collection("decks")` (5),
262	 * each deck `.doc(deckId)` below it (6) — building from a ref like
263	 * this keeps the parity right for you. Segments use letters, digits,
264	 * and `_ - . ~ : @ +` only (never `.` or `..` alone); at most
265	 * 200 bytes per segment, 1000 bytes and 16 segments per path.
266	 * `doc()`, `collection()` and the builders on refs THROW a
267	 * `TypeError` synchronously for a path that breaks
268	 * this grammar (its message names the broken rule; for parity, the
269	 * segment count) — a programming error to fix where the path is
270	 * written, not a store condition to handle; building a ref never
271	 * touches the network. Paths are data you choose — there is no need to
272	 * pre-create a collection, and deleting a document does NOT delete
273	 * documents nested under its path.
274	 *
275	 * The `data/users/` path prefix is special, platform-side: each
276	 * viewer's own subtree under it is private per viewer — including
277	 * from the artifact's owner (the default `data/users/{self}` rule;
278	 * a declared rule at the `data/users` prefix opens siblings' subtrees
279	 * at its levels, see ACCESS RULES above). Address the viewer's subtree as
280	 * `data/users/<id>/...` using the AWAITED value of
281	 * {@link Claude.user.id} (declare `user` alongside `db` — without
282	 * the declaration `id()` resolves null; it is async, and an
283	 * un-awaited promise is not a valid path segment, so the builder
284	 * throws) — the
285	 * store recognizes exactly that id as this viewer, no other value
286	 * works. A null id means no private subtree: disable the per-viewer
287	 * feature for that visit rather than relocating its data to a
288	 * shared path; a view-only or comment-only member has an id yet cannot
289	 * write there either, so treat a rejected write the same way. Another
290	 * viewer's documents under `data/users/`
291	 * read as non-existent (`exists: false`, omitted from queries and
292	 * `onSnapshot`) — the "shared by its viewers" default does NOT
293	 * apply inside this prefix — and a write (`set`/`update`/`delete`)
294	 * into another viewer's subtree rejects `invalid_argument`.
295	 * Hidden-until-reveal (sealed votes, planning poker): each viewer
296	 * writes their pick under their own `data/users/<id>/` path, where by
297	 * default nobody else can read it, and copies it to a shared path when
298	 * THEY reveal — rules are fixed at publish, so nothing a page does at
299	 * run time opens another viewer's subtree.
300	 */
301	
302	/** Snapshot provenance. `fromCache: true` marks a view the store has
303	 * not confirmed, such as a copy saved on an earlier visit, your own
304	 * writes before the first read lands, a collection too large to read
305	 * whole, or delivery during a connectivity gap. A definitive snapshot
306	 * follows by itself once the store answers in full.
307	 * `hasPendingWrites` is true while the view includes this page's own
308	 * unconfirmed write (latency compensation). */
309	type SnapshotMetadata = {
310	  fromCache: boolean;
311	  hasPendingWrites: boolean;
312	};
313	
314	/** One document, as reads and snapshots deliver it. Delivered
315	 *  snapshots and their `data()` are frozen; a document that didn't
316	 *  change is the same object across deliveries — compare with
317	 *  `===`, don't mutate or accumulate them (clone a body before
318	 *  editing it for a write). */
319	type DocumentSnapshot = {
320	  /** The last segment of the document's path. */
321	  id: string;
322	  /** False covers both a missing document and one this viewer cannot
323	   * see — deliberately indistinguishable. */
324	  exists: boolean;
325	  /** The document body; `undefined` when `exists` is false. */
326	  data(): Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
327	  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
328	};
329	
330	/** One ordered-view transition inside a query snapshot. Indexes are
331	 * positions in the snapshot's `docs` order: `oldIndex` is -1 for
332	 * `added`, `newIndex` is -1 for `removed`. `removed` covers
333	 * deletion, leaving the query, and losing visibility, identically; its
334	 * `doc` is the last snapshot the listener saw (`exists: true`,
335	 * carrying the final body), so a removal handler still has the data. */
336	type DocumentChange = {
337	  type: "added" | "modified" | "removed";
338	  doc: DocumentSnapshot;
339	  oldIndex: number;
340	  newIndex: number;
341	};
342	
343	/** A query's matched set, in query order. */
344	type QuerySnapshot = {
345	  docs: DocumentSnapshot[];
346	  size: number;
347	  empty: boolean;
348	  /** The changes since the previous snapshot of this listener (the
349	   * first snapshot is all-`added`). */
350	  docChanges(): DocumentChange[];
351	  metadata: SnapshotMetadata;
352	};
353	
354	/** Stop receiving snapshots. Idempotent; after it returns, the
355	 * callbacks never fire again. */
356	type Unsubscribe = () => void;
357	
358	type AcquireOptions = {
359	  /** Who holds the lease — any stable string (a viewer id, a tab
360	   * id). Renewal requires the same holder. */
361	  holder: string;
362	  /** Requested lease length in milliseconds. Absent/0 means 30000;
363	   * values are clamped to [1000, 600000], never rejected. */
364	  ttlMs?: number;
365	  /** Merged into the document body when the lease is granted. */
366	  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
367	};
368	
369	type AcquireResult = {
370	  acquired: boolean;
371	  /** The document's version after a granted acquire. */
372	  version?: number;
373	  /** RFC 3339 expiry of the lease now in force (granted or not). */
374	  expiresAt?: string;
375	  /** Your own holder string, echoed on a granted acquire; absent when
376	   * busy — the platform reveals `expiresAt`, never who holds it. */
377	  holder?: string;
378	};
379	
380	/**
381	 * A reference to one document. Pure and synchronous to create — a
382	 * malformed path throws here; nothing reaches the store until a
383	 * terminal call.
384	 */
385	type DocumentReference = {
386	  /** The last path segment. */
387	  id: string;
388	  path: string;
389	
390	  /** Read once. Absence is NOT an error — branch on `exists`. */
391	  get(): Promise<DocumentSnapshot>;
392	
393	  /** Write the WHOLE document, creating it (and the store) if
394	   * absent — a full replace, Firestore-style. Use `update` to merge
395	   * into existing fields. Writes are last-writer-wins; there are no
396	   * transactions.
397	   *
398	   * ONE WRITE AT A TIME per document, only when its data changed:
399	   * await each `set`/`update` before the next to the same document;
400	   * write on a user action or a real state change, never from render
401	   * code, a snapshot callback, or a timer that rewrites unchanged or
402	   * clock-derived values; coalesce a burst of input events into one
403	   * write per pause. The page open in other tabs or devices writes the
404	   * same documents; overlapping writes to one document make each write
405	   * slower. */
406	  set(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
407	
408	  /** Merge-write that REQUIRES the document to exist — rejects
409	   * `invalid_argument` otherwise (creating-on-miss would be a bug
410	   * for its use cases). Nested objects merge recursively; anything
411	   * else (arrays included) replaces that field wholesale. Same
412	   * one-write-at-a-time rule as `set`. Do NOT build monotonic
413	   * counters from read-modify-update — writes are last-writer-wins
414	   * and a retried write can apply twice. */
415	  update(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
416	
417	  /** Delete this document. Idempotent; nested documents survive. */
418	  delete(): Promise<void>;
419	
420	  /**
421	   * Cooperative short lease on this document — set-if-not-busy, the
422	   * single-writer primitive (one editor at a time, a migration that
423	   * should run once, a turn lock). NOT a security boundary: other
424	   * viewers can still write directly; leases only coordinate
425	   * callers that all use `acquire`. Busy resolves
426	   * `{acquired: false}` — a normal outcome, never an error. Leases
427	   * expire on their own (no release verb): prefer short `ttlMs`
428	   * and renew while working. There is no create-if-absent write, so
429	   * "claim a slot" (a seat, a username, first-come ownership) is:
430	   * `acquire` the slot document (short `ttlMs`, no `data`), `get()`
431	   * it, and while you hold the lease `set` your claim only if it does
432	   * not exist yet or its body names no owner, then let the lease
433	   * lapse; `{acquired: false}` means someone else is mid-claim — treat
434	   * the slot as taken or re-read after `expiresAt`. Do not carry the
435	   * claim in `acquire`'s `data` (it merges on every later grant too).
436	   * A bare get-then-set races and both callers believe they won.
437	   */
438	  acquire(options: AcquireOptions): Promise<AcquireResult>;
439	
440	  /**
441	   * Subscribe to this document. `next` fires with the current state
442	   * once the store answers, then on every change — including other
443	   * viewers' writes, live. Your own writes appear immediately
444	   * (`hasPendingWrites: true` until confirmed), and a returning viewer
445	   * may first get a copy saved on an earlier visit (`fromCache: true`).
446	   * Delivery rides a realtime stream when available and falls back to
447	   * periodic refresh (about 30 s foreground) — same callbacks either way.
448	   * While the store cannot be reached (offline, or a network that
449	   * holds, drops or blocks its requests) the listener may hear nothing
450	   * from it, not even an error, and keeps retrying until it answers.
451	   * So time-limit loading: start a timer of about 10 s when you
452	   * subscribe. If it fires, say the data can't be reached yet or, over
453	   * anything already delivered, that it may be out of date. The first
454	   * snapshot with `fromCache: false` clears the timer and that note; so
455	   * does `error`, which ends the loading state too. Until `error` fires,
456	   * keep the listener: never reload the page or subscribe again to
457	   * recover.
458	   * `error` receives at most one terminal {@link DbError}
459	   * (`invalid_argument`, `resource_exhausted`, `revoked`, or the
460	   * `unavailable` above), after which the subscription
461	   * is dead. Pass it: without one a terminal error is reported via
462	   * `reportError` (your `error` event and console see it) and the
463	   * listener still dies.
464	   *
465	   * SUBSCRIBE ONCE per document or query (when the view starts, or
466	   * when the path or filter really changes), keep the returned
467	   * `Unsubscribe`, and call it when done. Never subscribe from code
468	   * that runs on every render (a React component body, a `render()`
469	   * function, anything the snapshot callback triggers): each call
470	   * opens another subscription, each snapshot re-renders, and the
471	   * page loops. In React, subscribe in a `useEffect`, build the ref or
472	   * query inside it, depend only on stable primitives, and return the
473	   * unsubscribe. Don't omit the dependency list or put a query built
474	   * during render in it: either one re-subscribes on every render. To
475	   * sort or filter by fast-changing UI state, subscribe once to the
476	   * wider set and derive the view in render.
477	   */
478	  onSnapshot(
479	    next: (snap: DocumentSnapshot) => void,
480	    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
481	  ): Unsubscribe;
482	
483	  /** A subcollection under this document. */
484	  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
485	};
486	
487	/**
488	 * A filtered, ordered, limited view of one collection. Builders are
489	 * pure — each returns a NEW query; terminal calls do the work.
490	 * Filters and `orderBy` evaluate against top-level fields without
491	 * indexes (the store scans the collection), so keep queried
492	 * collections modest — hundreds to low thousands of documents.
493	 */
494	type Query = {
495	  /** Add a filter (up to 10). Operators: `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`,
496	   * `>`, `>=`, `in`, `not-in` (value arrays of at most 30), and
497	   * `array-contains`. */
498	  where(field: string, op: string, value: unknown): Query;
499	
500	  /** Order by one top-level field (at most one `orderBy`);
501	   * `dir` defaults to `"asc"`. Documents missing the field sort
502	   * last. Without `orderBy`, results are ordered by document id
503	   * (ascending) — the same on every delivery path. */
504	  orderBy(field: string, dir?: "asc" | "desc"): Query;
505	
506	  /** At most `n` documents (1-1000). An ordered, limited query is a
507	   * window: documents beyond the window are not delivered until
508	   * they enter it. */
509	  limit(n: number): Query;
510	
511	  /** Read the matched set once, in query order. */
512	  get(): Promise<QuerySnapshot>;
513	
514	  /** Subscribe to the matched set — same delivery contract and same
515	   * subscribe-once rule as {@link DocumentReference.onSnapshot} (in
516	   * React, subscribe inside the effect, never during render, and don't
517	   * list a query built during render as a dependency), with
518	   * `docChanges()` describing each transition. At most 64 active
519	   * subscriptions per view (the 65th rejects `resource_exhausted` on
520	   * the error callback). */
521	  onSnapshot(
522	    next: (snap: QuerySnapshot) => void,
523	    error?: (e: DbError) => void,
524	  ): Unsubscribe;
525	};
526	
527	/** A collection: a {@link Query} over everything in it, plus
528	 * document access and creation. */
529	type CollectionReference = Query & {
530	  path: string;
531	
532	  /** A document in this collection. Omit `id` to mint a fresh
533	   * client-generated id — the retriable-create idiom (the store has
534	   * no idempotency key; a retried create with a fresh ref leaves at
535	   * most one document per id). */
536	  doc(id?: string): DocumentReference;
537	
538	  /** Create a document under a client-generated id and resolve its
539	   * ref. Sugar for `.doc().set(data)`. */
540	  add(data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<DocumentReference>;
541	};
542	
543	/**
544	 * The store surface. Refs are pure path holders — building them never
545	 * touches the network; only the calls on them do.
546	 *
547	 * DOCUMENT BODIES are plain-JSON OBJECTS (not arrays or scalars at
548	 * the top level): at most 256 KiB serialized and 32 levels deep.
549	 * CAPACITY: an artifact's database holds at most 25,000 documents in
550	 * total. Don't map an unbounded, growing stream (events, log lines,
551	 * messages) to one document per item — aggregate many items into one
552	 * document or prune old ones — and when a create rejects with
553	 * `quota_exceeded`, tell the viewer what happened and what to do.
554	 * Numbers are JSON numbers (double precision). Writes are
555	 * last-writer-wins — compare document STATE to reason about
556	 * concurrency, never row counts or call counts.
557	 */
558	type DB = {
559	  /** A document reference. The path must have an even number of
560	   * segments (`tasks/t1`); throws `TypeError` for a path that breaks
561	   * the grammar above. */
562	  doc(path: string): DocumentReference;
563	
564	  /** A collection reference. The path must have an odd number of
565	   * segments (`tasks`, `boards/b1/columns`); throws `TypeError` for a
566	   * path that breaks the grammar above. */
567	  collection(path: string): CollectionReference;
568	};
569	
570	interface ClaudeCapabilityMap {
571	  db: DB;
572	}
573

1	/**
2	 * `claude.use(name)` — the one way to reach a capability.
3	 *
4	 *   const db = await claude.use("db");
5	 *   if (!db) return renderWithoutDb(); // design for absence
6	 *   db.collection("tasks").onSnapshot(render);
7	 *
8	 * Resolves the capability's namespace once this view can run the
9	 * capability's code, or `null` when it cannot: the capability is not
10	 * served on this view, was not granted at initialization, or its module
11	 * failed to load. The null cases are indistinguishable by design —
12	 * design for absence, exactly as `permissions.state()` documents. (Chat
13	 * artifacts use a different, flat `window.claude`; neither `use()` nor
14	 * these namespaces exist there.)
15	 *
16	 * Timing. Inside a viewer the page is framed and `window.claude` exists
17	 * before any of your script runs. Served top-level by the platform, as
18	 * its own page on the artifact's own host, it has the same `use`-only
19	 * `window.claude` before your script too, and every `use()` resolves
20	 * `null` there for now; any other top-level copy of the page (a saved
21	 * file, another host) has no `window.claude` at all. This contract
22	 * promises nothing on it but `use`: treat `window.claude.db`,
23	 * `window.claude.room` and every other capability member as `undefined`
24	 * at every moment. The namespace arrives later, through the promise, once
25	 * the viewer has answered and the module has loaded — never during your
26	 * script's first synchronous run, and not ordered against
27	 * `DOMContentLoaded` either way, so don't assume the DOM is complete
28	 * when it resolves. Render the page without it and light features up
29	 * when it resolves. Framed by a host that never answers, it resolves
30	 * `null` after 10 s.
31	 *
32	 * The resolved namespace is platform-owned and read-only: a frozen
33	 * object whose members are the capability's functions. Call them and
34	 * keep the reference; assigning to it, `Object.defineProperty` on it,
35	 * or replacing a member throws (or silently does nothing). For helpers
36	 * of your own, wrap it in your own object.
37	 *
38	 * `use()` answers one question: can this view run the capability's
39	 * code? Permission stays on the calls themselves — a consent prompt,
40	 * rate limit, or policy refusal arrives on the first call, never here.
41	 * For a capability this view serves the promise is memoized — every
42	 * `use("db")` yields the same promise object; a name not served
43	 * resolves `null` (with no stable promise identity).
44	 */
45	interface ClaudeCapabilityMap {}
46	
47	interface Claude {
48	  /**
49	   * See {@link ClaudeCapabilityMap} for the names `use()` accepts on
50	   * this contract version; an unknown name is a compile error in typed
51	   * authoring and resolves `null` at runtime.
52	   */
53	  use<K extends keyof ClaudeCapabilityMap & string>(
54	    name: K,
55	  ): Promise<ClaudeCapabilityMap[K] | null>;
56	}

59	// `interface ClaudeCapabilityMap` in your own contract.d.ts — one line,
60	// same declaration-merging pattern as `interface Claude`.
61	interface Window {
62	  claude: Claude;
63	}

 ﻿function Test-MtEntraUnremediatedHighRiskUser {
-    <#
-    .SYNOPSIS
-    Finds users that Entra ID Protection rates high risk and that nobody has remediated.
-    .DESCRIPTION
-    Entra ID Protection flags users it believes are compromised and assigns a risk level and a
-    risk state. A flag only clears when someone remediates it (password reset) or an admin
-    dismisses or confirms-safe it. This check reports users whose risk level is high and whose

@@ -74,10 +59,64 @@

+    # Privileged users at risk raise severity to High (#2518). Roles are only read when there is
+    # something to report, so a clean tenant makes no extra Graph calls. The role lookup is extra
+    # detail: if it fails, the unremediated users are still reported, with a note.
+    $PrivilegedRolesByUser = @{}
+    $RoleNote = ''
+    try {
+        $RoleDefinitions = @(
+            Invoke-MtGraphRequest -ApiVersion 'v1.0' `
+                -RelativeUri 'roleManagement/directory/roleDefinitions' `
+                -Select @('id', 'displayName')
+        )
+        $RoleDefLookup = @{}
+        foreach ($Def in $RoleDefinitions) { $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Def.id] = $Def }
+
+        # Same properties as MT.1209 and MT.1210 so the active assignments come from the Graph cache.
+        $RoleAssignmentResult = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -Select @('id', 'principalId', 'roleDefinitionId', 'directoryScopeId')
+        if (!$RoleAssignmentResult.EligibleChecked) {
+            $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: PIM-eligible role assignments were not checked because they need " +
+                'Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance. Only active role assignments were checked.'
+        }
+
+        $UnremediatedIds = @{}
+        foreach ($Item in $Unremediated) { $UnremediatedIds[[string]$Item.id] = $true }
+
+        foreach ($Assignment in @($RoleAssignmentResult.Assignments)) {
+            $PrincipalId = [string]$Assignment.principalId
+            if (!$UnremediatedIds.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) { continue }
+            $RoleDef = $RoleDefLookup[[string]$Assignment.roleDefinitionId]
+            if ($null -eq $RoleDef) { continue }
+            # isPrivileged is not queryable on roleDefinitions; use Maester's role catalog, as MT.1210 does.
+            $RoleInfo = Get-MtRoleInfo -RoleName ([string]$RoleDef.displayName -replace '\s', '')

+            if (!$PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey($PrincipalId)) {
+                $PrivilegedRolesByUser[$PrincipalId] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
+            }
+            $PrivilegedRolesByUser[$PrincipalId].Add($RoleName)
+        }
+    } catch {

+        $RoleNote = "`n`nNote: Directory role assignments could not be read, so privileged users were not identified."
+    }
+
+    # Privileged users first, then by user principal name.
+    $Sorted = @(
+        $Unremediated | Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { -not $PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) } }, userPrincipalName
+    )
+    $PrivilegedCount = @($Unremediated | Where-Object { $PrivilegedRolesByUser.ContainsKey([string]$_.id) }).Count
+
     $Result = "Found $($Unremediated.Count) high-risk user(s) with unremediated risk."
-    $Result += "`n`n| User | User principal name | Risk state | Risk detail | Risk last updated |"
-    $Result += "`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"
-    foreach ($Item in $Unremediated) {

+    $Result += "`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"

@@ -87,9 +126,17 @@
         $Updated = if ($Item.riskLastUpdatedDateTime) {

﻿High-risk users should not be left unremediated in Entra ID Protection.

Entra ID Protection rates a user's risk and tracks a risk state for each flagged user. A high-risk flag only clears when the risk is remediated, for example by a password reset, or when an admin dismisses it or confirms the user safe. Until then the account stays exposed: the signals that triggered the flag have not been addressed.

This check reports users whose risk level is **high** and whose risk state is still active and unremediated (`atRisk` or `confirmedCompromised`). States that represent a handled flag (`remediated`, `dismissed`, `confirmedSafe`, `none`) are not reported. The check reads risk only and never changes a user's risk state.

data.author: dustinscholl
data.summary: Reads the tenant's baseline scopes choice from `identity/conditionalAccess/settings` (beta) and fails when enforcement is disabled or a policy excludes Windows Azure Active Directory. Logic matches Microsoft Learn; 21 unit tests cover every branch. Only conflict is `selection.json`.

findings.text: No stored selection returns Investigate. Microsoft's FAQ says enforcement is turned on by the rollout when nobody chooses, and the settings page then shows no selection, so most tenants would be flagged permanently.
Title says enforcement "should be enabled", but a tenant with it enabled can still fail on the Windows Azure Active Directory exclusion.
Disable enforcement fails even when no policy is exposed. Defensible as hardening.

fixes.text: Merge main into the branch and regenerate `selection.json` with `./build/golden/Export-MtGoldenFixture.ps1`

data.comment:
Thanks @dustinscholl, this is a solid check. The logic matches Microsoft's guidance on baseline scopes, and the tests cover every branch.

One change before we merge:
- **No stored selection** (`Test.MT.1259.ps1:112-116`): when nobody makes a choice, Microsoft's rollout turns enforcement on and it becomes the default, while the settings page still shows no selection. Most tenants will be in that state and would get Investigate permanently. Could this case pass with a note, and only return Investigate while an enabled policy targets All resources with an exclusion?

Optional:
- The title says enforcement "should be enabled", but a tenant with enforcement on can still fail on the Windows Azure Active Directory exclusion. Something like "Baseline scopes should be enforced by Conditional Access" covers both.

We'll merge main into your branch and regenerate `selection.json`, so you don't need to deal with the conflict.

data.title: Align 2.1.x CIS checks with benchmark procedures
data.author: JeremyFinney-lgtm
data.summary: Reworks the CIS 2.1.x Defender for Office 365 / EOP checks. It fixes a real false pass in 2.1.1 and adds fail-closed paths, but changes which policy most checks evaluate. 2.1.7 gets much stricter, while 2.1.11 and 2.1.15 get looser.
data.question: Accept 2.1.11 passing at 90% file-type coverage (main requires 100%), and 2.1.15 checking only the Default outbound policy (main also checks custom policies)? The draft asks the author to justify both from the v7 audit text.
data.ciNote: Same stale `test-builder.json` on main as #2618; not this PR's fault.

findings.text: 2.1.7: Strict and Standard preset anti-phishing policies have no `AntiPhishRule` (their rules are `EOPProtectionPolicyRule`/`ATPProtectionPolicyRule`), so a tenant on the Strict preset fails.
2.1.15 drops custom outbound policies applied by enabled rules, so a weaker custom policy passes. Inconsistent with 2.1.6, which now follows custom policies on the same object.
2.1.4 / 2.1.7: any group target passes scope while user targets fail, and exclusions are ignored.
2.1.11: the new 90% threshold needs a citation to the v7 audit procedure.
2.1.11 matches rules on `Id` only; 2.1.3 matches Id, Name and Identity.

Behaviour moves in 2.1.3, 2.1.4 and 2.1.6 (highest-priority custom policy instead of Default); stricter in 2.1.1, 2.1.5, 2.1.9, 2.1.12-2.1.14. Follow-up: CISA MS.EXO.12.1/12.2 duplicate 2.1.12/2.1.13 and could become shims.

fixes.text: Make 2.1.11 match rules on Id, Name and Identity, as 2.1.3 does

data.comment:
Thanks for working through the whole 2.1.x section, @JeremyFinney-lgtm. Fixing the false pass in 2.1.1 and the fail-closed paths is a real improvement. A few things before we can merge:

- **2.1.7**: Strict and Standard preset anti-phishing policies have no `AntiPhishRule`; their rules are `EOPProtectionPolicyRule`/`ATPProtectionPolicyRule`. A tenant using the Strict preset will fail. Please treat an enabled preset as a candidate.
- **2.1.15**: dropping custom policies applied by enabled rules lets a weaker custom policy pass. 2.1.6 now follows custom policies on the same outbound policy object, so the two disagree. Could you keep the custom-policy evaluation, or point to the v7 audit text that limits it to Default?
- **2.1.11**: can you cite where the v7 audit procedure sets the 90% coverage threshold? Main required full coverage. Please also match rules on Id, Name and Identity, as 2.1.3 does.
- **2.1.4 / 2.1.7 scope**: any group target passes while user targets fail, and exclusions are ignored. Please either evaluate both the same way or report scope without passing or failing on it.
- Please run the full `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. The current CI failure is a stale `test-builder.json` on main, not your change, so we'll fix that separately.

data.title: Add CIS 1.1.4 and broaden admin-role coverage
data.author: JeremyFinney-lgtm
data.summary: Adds CIS 1.1.4 (admins hold identity-only licences) and widens the role list in 1.1.1. It also changes the exported `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` so a failed batch subrequest throws, which breaks other checks and users' custom tests.
data.ciNote: Fails on the PR itself: `selection.json` and `test-builder.json` weren't regenerated for 1.1.4.

findings.text: `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` (public API): any non-2xx batch subrequest now throws. One stale ID errors CIS 1.2.2, CISA MS.AAD.7.3, MT.1074, MT.1197 and any custom test passing several `-UniqueId` values. 1.1.1 doesn't need it.

1.1.4 runs only with delegated sign-in, so it skips app-only runs. Listing `licenseDetails` should work with application permissions, and `assignedLicenses` plus `subscribedSkus` avoids one request per user.
1.1.4 doesn't check for missing users, so a missing admin is skipped and the check can pass.
Mitre `T1566.002` fails the rubric: the guide covers attachments, links and service (three sub-techniques), so it should be `T1566`.
`Test.CIS.M365.1.1.4.md` has no trailing newline.

data.comment:
Thanks @JeremyFinney-lgtm for adding 1.1.4 and widening the role list in 1.1.1.

Changes needed:
- **`Invoke-MtGraphRequest`** is a public command used by many checks and by users' custom tests. With this change, one failed batch subrequest (a 404 for a stale ID, say) throws and fails the whole call, where it used to return the error and carry on. That changes CIS 1.2.2, CISA MS.AAD.7.3, MT.1074 and MT.1197. 1.1.1 already handles missing users itself, so please revert this file here. The 429/5xx retry is welcome as its own PR, keeping 404s returned as before or behind an opt-in switch.
- **1.1.4 skips app-only runs.** As far as I can tell, listing `licenseDetails` works with application permissions. Reading `assignedLicenses` in the existing batch and mapping SKUs through `subscribedSkus` would work in both modes and avoid one request per user.
- **1.1.4 doesn't report missing users** the way 1.1.1 now does, so a missing admin is skipped and the check can pass.
- **Mitre**: the guide covers phishing by attachment, link and service, so per the rubric this should be the parent `T1566`, not `T1566.002`.
- **CI**: after merging main, regenerate `selection.json` (`./build/golden/Export-MtGoldenFixture.ps1`) and `website/src/data/test-builder.json` (`./build/website/Update-MtTestBuilderData.ps1`).

input.content:
---
name: maester-pr-desk
description: Merill's PR review desk for maester365/maester. Use when he asks to "review the new PRs", "update the PR desk", "check which PRs can merge", or "process the PR desk" (act on what he queued). Reviews open PRs, writes a verdict, findings, maintainer fixes and a draft comment for each into the PR Desk artifact, then, once he queues decisions there, posts the reviews, pushes the fixes and merges.
---

# Maester PR Desk

The desk is a published artifact with a small database:
**https://claude.ai/artifact/UohxsGPhGM6VveP4w7ayvo**

The page source is `pr-desk.html`, in this folder. To change the page, edit that file and publish it with the Artifact tool and that `url`; read the artifact first in a new conversation. Read and write its data with the `ArtifactData` tool, using the same `url`.

There are two modes. Merill says which one he wants.

## Mode 1: review ("review the new PRs", "update the desk")

1. **List.** Run `gh pr list --state open` for maester365/maester. Skip drafts; at most, mention them in one line.
   - `ArtifactData list prs` shows what is already on the desk.
   - Review a PR again only if it is new, or its head SHA differs from `prs/<n>.headSha`.
   - If a PR has merged or closed, set `verdict` to `merged` or `closed` and keep its doc as history.
2. **Review.** Fetch each PR's head as `refs/remotes/pr/<n>`: `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`. Never check out over Merill's working branch.
   - Read the existing review threads first, so you don't repeat points that are resolved.
   - Do small PRs inline. Send larger ones to `maester-test-expert` subagents in parallel, read-only.
   - Ask each subagent for: a verdict, the CI cause and fix, behaviour changes against main, findings with file:line, a draft comment, and fixes a maintainer could make.
   - Apply AGENTS.md: the attribute rubric, repository layout, generated files, and benchmark shims. Also check for changes to exported public commands.
   - **Verify the one or two claims that matter** before they go into a comment. For example, read the diff for a "breaking change", or look up Graph permissions with the `msgraph` skill. Don't relay subagent claims unchecked.
   - Check whether CI failures are the PR's fault or come from main. A stale generated file on main is a common cause: `test-builder.json`, `selection.json`, or a broken docs link.
3. **Write** one `prs/<number>` doc per PR, all in a single `ArtifactData batch`, using the schema below.
4. **Report** in chat: a short line per PR, and the desk link. Don't post anything to GitHub in this mode.

## Mode 2: act ("process the PR desk")

1. Run `ArtifactData list decisions` and pick the docs where `status == "queued"`. Ignore `draft` and `hold`.
2. For each one, before acting:
   - If `decision.prSha` or `prs.headSha` differs from the PR's current head on GitHub, stop for that PR. Re-review it, update its doc, set the decision back to `draft` with a note in `prs.outcome`, and tell Merill.
   - Make sure the comment still matches the fixes he ticked. If he unticked a fix that the comment says "I pushed", remove that sentence, or ask him.
3. **Fixes:** apply each ticked `fixes[].id` on the contributor's branch.
   - Use a worktree under the scratchpad, never the main checkout. The PR must have `maintainerCanModify` set.
   - Prefer merging main to rebasing, so you never force-push over a contributor's history.
   - Regenerate generated files with their build scripts, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before pushing.
   - The commit message ends with the session's Co-Authored-By line.
   - A fix that targets main, like `builder-main`, becomes its own branch and PR off main.
4. **Review:** `event` APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT → `gh pr review <n> --approve|--request-changes|--comment --body-file <file>`. `NONE` → post nothing.
   - The comment is Merill's text, edited on the desk. Post it word for word.
5. **Merge:** only if `merge` is true and CI is green on the commit you just pushed. Use `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   - Never enable auto-merge. If CI is still running, leave the PR and say so.
6. **Record:** update `decisions/<n>` to `status: "done"` with `doneAt`, and `prs/<n>.outcome` with one line on what happened, including links or SHAs.
   - Pin each write to the version you read, with `if_version`.
7. **Report** in chat what was posted, pushed and merged, and anything you skipped and why.

## Data schema

`prs/<number>` is written by Claude:
- **Identity:** `number`, `title`, `author`, `url`, `headSha` (12 chars), `size` (`"+a/-d · n files"`).
- **State:** `merge` (`mergeable|conflicting|behind|blocked`), `ci` (`passing|failing|pending`), `ciNote`.
- **Verdict:** `verdict` (`ready|small-fix|changes|decision|merged|closed`), `order` (rank: ready first, then by complexity).
- **Review:** `reviewedAt` (ISO), `summary`, and `question`, used only when Merill must rule on something.
- **Findings:** `findings[]`, each `{sev: high|medium|low|nit, text, where}`.
- **Fixes:** `fixes[]`, each `{id, text, preselect}`. These are things we could do on the branch ourselves.
- **Draft:** `event` (`APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT|NONE`) and `comment`, which is markdown for GitHub.
- **History:** `outcome`, a one-line log of the last action.

`decisions/<number>` is written by the page:
- **Review:** `comment`, `event`, `fixes[]` (ticked ids), `merge` (bool).
- **State:** `status` (`draft|queued|hold|done`), `prSha`, `decidedAt`, and `doneAt`, which Claude sets.

Inline text renders `` `code` `` and `**bold**`.

## Writing the comment

- Address the author with their real @login, and thank them once.
- Plain English, short bullets, and bold labels for the blocking items. No emoji, and no headings beyond bold.
- Say clearly what blocks the merge and what is optional.
- When CI fails because of main, tell them it isn't their fault and that we'll fix it.
- Say "I pushed …" only for fixes that will actually be ticked and pushed.

## Process notes

Merill's rulings go here as they come up.

- Skip contributors' draft PRs.
- Read the existing reviews before reviewing.
- A benchmark test that duplicates another suite's check is a shim.
- No "(Preview)" in test titles.

content.text:
The CIS v7 PDF contradicts itself here, and you and the PR author are each following a different part of it. I read 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2, 5.2.2.5 and 5.2.2.8 in `~/Downloads/REDACTED.0.0.pdf`:

| | UI audit | Graph API audit | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **5.2.2.1** admins MFA | All resources, no exclusions | `IncludeApplications` is All; excluded apps not checked | Don't create any exclusions |
| **5.2.2.2** all users MFA | All resources, no exclusions | `IncludeApplications` is All; excluded apps not checked | Don't create any exclusions |
| **5.2.2.5** phishing-resistant MFA for admins | All resources, no exclusions | `IncludeApplications` is All; excluded apps not checked | No exclusions other than break-glass accounts |
| **5.2.2.8** block medium/high sign-in risk | All resources, no exclusions | Also requires "ExcludeApplications is null or empty" | No exclusions |

- **Main** (your commit `895aca9e2`) follows the UI audit and remediation: any excluded app fails 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2 and 5.2.2.5.
- **#2600** follows the Graph API audit literally. Those three steps check only that all apps are included, and only 5.2.2.8 also checks for excluded apps. So the PR drops the exclusion condition from the first three and keeps it on 5.2.2.8.
- **5.2.2.2's Impact section recommends one exclusion.** If external users have trouble opening documents protected by sensitivity labels, it suggests excluding Microsoft Rights Management Services (`00000012-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`). Main's strict check fails a tenant that follows that advice.

Both readings can point to text in the benchmark. Since 5.2.2.8's Graph steps add the excluded-apps check and the other three don't, the omission may be deliberate. It may also be an oversight, given that the UI audit says otherwise.

**My recommendation: a middle ground.**
- Keep failing on application exclusions, because two of the three procedures say there should be none.
- In 5.2.2.2, allow the Rights Management Services app, since CIS itself recommends that exclusion.
- List any excluded apps in the result, so an admin can see what was found.

If you agree, I'll rewrite the #2600 card around that, with a comment that cites these audit steps, before you queue it.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/merill/.claude/skills/maester-pr-desk

# Maester PR Desk

The desk is a published artifact with a small database:
**https://claude.ai/artifact/UohxsGPhGM6VveP4w7ayvo**

The page source is `pr-desk.html`, in this folder. To change the page, edit that file and publish it with the Artifact tool and that `url`; read the artifact first in a new conversation. Read and write its data with the `ArtifactData` tool, using the same `url`.

There are two modes. Merill says which one he wants.

## Mode 1: review ("review the new PRs", "update the desk")

1. **List.** Run `gh pr list --state open` for maester365/maester. Skip drafts; at most, mention them in one line.
   - `ArtifactData list prs` shows what is already on the desk.
   - Review a PR again only if it is new, or its head SHA differs from `prs/<n>.headSha`.
   - If a PR has merged or closed, set `verdict` to `merged` or `closed` and keep its doc as history.
2. **Review.** Fetch each PR's head as `refs/remotes/pr/<n>`: `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head:refs/remotes/pr/<n>`. Never check out over Merill's working branch.
   - Read the existing review threads first, so you don't repeat points that are resolved.
   - Do small PRs inline. Send larger ones to `maester-test-expert` subagents in parallel, read-only.
   - Ask each subagent for: a verdict, the CI cause and fix, behaviour changes against main, findings with file:line, a draft comment, and fixes a maintainer could make.
   - Apply AGENTS.md: the attribute rubric, repository layout, generated files, and benchmark shims. Also check for changes to exported public commands.
   - **Verify the one or two claims that matter** before they go into a comment. For example, read the diff for a "breaking change", or look up Graph permissions with the `msgraph` skill. Don't relay subagent claims unchecked.
   - Check whether CI failures are the PR's fault or come from main. A stale generated file on main is a common cause: `test-builder.json`, `selection.json`, or a broken docs link.
3. **Write** one `prs/<number>` doc per PR, all in a single `ArtifactData batch`, using the schema below.
4. **Report** in chat: a short line per PR, and the desk link. Don't post anything to GitHub in this mode.

## Mode 2: act ("process the PR desk")

1. Run `ArtifactData list decisions` and pick the docs where `status == "queued"`. Ignore `draft` and `hold`.
2. For each one, before acting:
   - If `decision.prSha` or `prs.headSha` differs from the PR's current head on GitHub, stop for that PR. Re-review it, update its doc, set the decision back to `draft` with a note in `prs.outcome`, and tell Merill.
   - Make sure the comment still matches the fixes he ticked. If he unticked a fix that the comment says "I pushed", remove that sentence, or ask him.
3. **Fixes:** apply each ticked `fixes[].id` on the contributor's branch.
   - Use a worktree under the scratchpad, never the main checkout. The PR must have `maintainerCanModify` set.
   - Prefer merging main to rebasing, so you never force-push over a contributor's history.
   - Regenerate generated files with their build scripts, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before pushing.
   - The commit message ends with the session's Co-Authored-By line.
   - A fix that targets main, like `builder-main`, becomes its own branch and PR off main.
4. **Review:** `event` APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT → `gh pr review <n> --approve|--request-changes|--comment --body-file <file>`. `NONE` → post nothing.
   - The comment is Merill's text, edited on the desk. Post it word for word.
5. **Merge:** only if `merge` is true and CI is green on the commit you just pushed. Use `gh pr merge <n> --merge`.
   - Never enable auto-merge. If CI is still running, leave the PR and say so.
6. **Record:** update `decisions/<n>` to `status: "done"` with `doneAt`, and `prs/<n>.outcome` with one line on what happened, including links or SHAs.
   - Pin each write to the version you read, with `if_version`.
7. **Report** in chat what was posted, pushed and merged, and anything you skipped and why.

## Data schema

`prs/<number>` is written by Claude:
- **Identity:** `number`, `title`, `author`, `url`, `headSha` (12 chars), `size` (`"+a/-d · n files"`).
- **State:** `merge` (`mergeable|conflicting|behind|blocked`), `ci` (`passing|failing|pending`), `ciNote`.
- **Verdict:** `verdict` (`ready|small-fix|changes|decision|merged|closed`), `order` (rank: ready first, then by complexity).
- **Review:** `reviewedAt` (ISO), `summary`, and `question`, used only when Merill must rule on something.
- **Findings:** `findings[]`, each `{sev: high|medium|low|nit, text, where}`.
- **Fixes:** `fixes[]`, each `{id, text, preselect}`. These are things we could do on the branch ourselves.
- **Draft:** `event` (`APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT|NONE`) and `comment`, which is markdown for GitHub.
- **History:** `outcome`, a one-line log of the last action.

`decisions/<number>` is written by the page:
- **Review:** `comment`, `event`, `fixes[]` (ticked ids), `merge` (bool).
- **State:** `status` (`draft|queued|hold|done`), `prSha`, `decidedAt`, and `doneAt`, which Claude sets.

Inline text renders `` `code` `` and `**bold**`.

## Writing the comment

- Address the author with their real @login, and thank them once.
- Plain English, short bullets, and bold labels for the blocking items. No emoji, and no headings beyond bold.
- Say clearly what blocks the merge and what is optional.
- When CI fails because of main, tell them it isn't their fault and that we'll fix it.
- Say "I pushed …" only for fixes that will actually be ticked and pushed.

## Process notes

Merill's rulings go here as they come up.

- Skip contributors' draft PRs.
- Read the existing reviews before reviewing.
- A benchmark test that duplicates another suite's check is a shim.
- No "(Preview)" in test titles.

--- comment:
Thanks @JeremyFinney-lgtm. The 5.2.2.9 and 5.2.2.10 wording is clearer, and the new OR/AND operator tests are a good addition.

On application exclusions in 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2 and 5.2.2.5, I see where this comes from: the v7 Graph API audit for those three only checks that `IncludeApplications` is All. The UI audit for the same recommendations says All resources must be selected with no exclusions, and the remediation says not to create any. 5.2.2.8's Graph audit also checks that `ExcludeApplications` is empty. Two of the three procedures say no exclusions, so we'd like to keep that as the rule.

Could you:
- **Keep the `No excluded applications` condition** in 5.2.2.1, 5.2.2.2 and 5.2.2.5.
- **Allow one exception in 5.2.2.2**: Microsoft Rights Management Services (`00000012-0000-0000-c000-000000000000`). The benchmark's Impact section for 5.2.2.2 recommends excluding it so external users can open documents protected by sensitivity labels.
- **List the excluded apps in the result**, so an admin can see what was found and why the check failed.
- Update the guides and the unit tests to match, including the one named "passes … for manual review".

The rest of the PR is good to go as it is.

--- comment:
Thanks @JeremyFinney-lgtm for adding 1.1.4 and widening the role list in 1.1.1.

Changes needed:
- **`Invoke-MtGraphRequest`** is a public command used by many checks and by users' custom tests. With this change, one failed batch subrequest (a 404 for a stale ID, say) throws and fails the whole call, where it used to return the error and carry on. That changes CIS 1.2.2, CISA MS.AAD.7.3, MT.1074 and MT.1197. 1.1.1 already handles missing users itself, so please revert this file here. The 429/5xx retry is welcome as its own PR, keeping 404s returned as before or behind an opt-in switch.
- **1.1.4 skips app-only runs.** As far as I can tell, listing `licenseDetails` works with application permissions. Reading `assignedLicenses` in the existing batch and mapping SKUs through `subscribedSkus` would work in both modes and avoid one request per user.
- **1.1.4 doesn't report missing users** the way 1.1.1 now does, so a missing admin is skipped and the check can pass.
- **Mitre**: the guide covers phishing by attachment, link and service, so per the rubric this should be the parent `T1566`, not `T1566.002`.
- **CI**: after merging main, regenerate `selection.json` (`./build/golden/Export-MtGoldenFixture.ps1`) and `website/src/data/test-builder.json` (`./build/website/Update-MtTestBuilderData.ps1`).

fix(github): assess existing CIS deletion checks with approved users
06691925fa53378dfcf7f5ff51cfb5b2e2a099d6
## Description

This updates the five existing CIS checks for GitHub organization settings. For deletion permissions, checking whether deletion is enabled or disabled isn't enough to meet the benchmark. The checks also need to identify who has that access and whether those users have been explicitly approved as trusted and qualified.

The changes cover the following:

- **When member deletion is disabled:** Check the number of distinct organization owners and compare them against `ApprovedOwnerIds` and `MaximumOrganizationOwners`. Approvals apply to the specific GitHub host and organization. The default maximum is 3 owners, configurable from 1 to 3. CIS refers to a "few" owners without defining a number, so this limit is Maester's interpretation.
- **When member deletion is enabled:** Require exactly two approved users with effective administrator access to each repository. Collect the users visible through the API even when approvals haven't been configured. To pass, the assessment still needs a complete repository inventory declared independently of that discovery, along with complete evidence of administrator access and approvals.
- **When information is missing or conflicts:** Keep confirmed count or approval failures even if other inventory or approval information is missing. Count matching duplicates once. Conflicting repository identities or contradictory administrator permissions cannot establish a result. Missing approvals display Not configured and don't imply that a user is approved or disapproved.
- **When other permissions or policies affect deletion:** Check the evidence of restrictive policies when determining whether repository deletion violates the benchmark. For issue deletion, unresolved permissions from additional custom roles require investigation even if the assessment would otherwise pass. If an execution error occurs, retain the sanitized observations collected so far and report Error ahead of any configuration result.
- **For repository creation, team creation, and base permissions:** Correct how the checks assess the setting values and their data types. For repository creation, either public or private creation being enabled is enough to fail. Both values must be Boolean false to pass.
- **For API requests:** Reuse the shared read-only REST/GraphQL handling for evidence collection, pagination, cache isolation, request routing, and rate limits. New REST evidence requests use API version `2026-03-10`; connection defaults remain unchanged. Every assessment request now uses the existing 30-second limits for connection/header waits and stalled response-body reads, without automatic retries. These limits apply to those waits, not to the total assessment time.
- **For redacted exports:** Support the optional `Add-MtTestResultDetail -RedactedResult` parameter to provide complete result Markdown with user identities replaced by pseudonyms. Copy results before exporting so the caller's original results are preserved. Selected exports protect user identities even when the generic identity map is empty. Approval configuration is treated as sensitive and excluded from exported configuration.

No new CIS check IDs or classification attributes are introduced. The documentation makes clear which requirements come from CIS, which owner limit is Maester's policy, which approvals the assessor must provide, and where API evidence is incomplete.

## Validation

Local validation uses pinned Pester 5.7.1 on Linux:

- Twelve regression tests for previously missed findings fail against the unchanged reviewed version, `5710ed8039a8728f35e0ad3534cdb6a56aaa7d4a`. The updated assessment and inventory test suites pass all 138 cases.
- Tests for running the checks and exporting results from source, including redacted-result validation, pass all 39 cases. Tests against the built module, covering check execution, exports, and real HTTP timeouts, pass all 29 cases. All five checks are discovered as valid.

=== 1.2.2
﻿Organization members cannot create public or private repositories.

Limiting repository creation makes ownership and access easier to review and reduces the risk of code or data being exposed through an unmanaged repository. Members who need a new repository may need an owner, administrator, or approved internal process to create it.

CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 lists section 1.2.2 as a Manual assessment. This test checks the connected organization's repository-creation settings from `GET /orgs/{org}`; it does not replace the rest of the manual review.

The test passes when `members_can_create_public_repositories` and `members_can_create_private_repositories` are both Boolean `false`. Either value being Boolean `true` is enough to fail, even if the other value is missing or invalid. Otherwise, a missing, null, or non-Boolean value produces **Skipped**, with a reason explaining what could not be checked. Request or JSON parsing failures produce **Error**.

The report also shows `members_can_create_internal_repositories` and the legacy `members_allowed_repository_creation_type` when GitHub returns them. Neither decides the result: the CIS audit covers public and private repository creation, and Maester uses the separate settings for those repository types.

The test covers the connected organization's returned settings. It does not scan other organizations or reconstruct inherited policies. Maester checks these fields after parsing the response, rather than validating the entire response schema. Missing data does not mean a setting is disabled or the recommendation does not apply.

#### Permissions required

Use an organization owner with a classic PAT or OAuth token carrying `admin:org` to read the full organization settings. With fine-grained PATs, the connection's membership check uses organization **Members: read**, and its separate administration check uses **Administration: read**. A successful connection does not guarantee that GitHub returns the fields this test needs. See [Connect-MtGitHub](https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Connect-MtGitHub) for the connection checks.

For GHE.com, use `https://api.SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com` and a token for that host; do not assume the github.com device flow applies. The same missing-data rules apply to GHEC, Enterprise Managed Users, and GHE.com.

#### Remediation action

1. On the connected GitHub web host (`github.com` or your enterprise's `SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com`), open **Your organizations**, select the organization, then go to **Settings** > **Access** > **Member privileges**.
2. Clear the public and private repository-creation options for members and save the changes. If an enterprise policy controls the options, ask an enterprise owner to make the change.
3. Review internal repository creation separately; it does not decide this check.

#### Related links

* [CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 - Section 1.2.2](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/github)
* [GitHub: Restricting repository creation](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/organizations/managing-organization-settings/restricting-repository-creation-in-your-organization)
* [GitHub REST API: Get an organization](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/rest/orgs/orgs?apiVersion=2026-03-10#get-an-organization)

=== 1.2.3
Repository deletion is limited to the owners or repository administrators your organization has approved.

Deleting a repository removes code, development history, and evidence of accidental or malicious activity. Keep deletion access with a small group of trusted and qualified users, and use an approved process to retire repositories. Other users may need an owner or administrator to delete a repository for them.

CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 lists section 1.2.3 as a Manual assessment. Your organization decides which users are trusted and qualified; Maester compares your approvals with the owners and administrators returned by GitHub.

Configure `GlobalSettings.GitHubDeletionPolicy` in `maester-config.json` as described in [GitHub deletion approvals](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/github-deletion-policy). The test follows the organization's `members_can_delete_repositories` setting:

- When member deletion is disabled, every organization owner must be approved, and the number of owners must not exceed `MaximumOrganizationOwners`. The default is **3**, configurable from **1 through 3**. This is Maester's interpretation of "few"; CIS does not specify a number.
- When member deletion is enabled, every repository must have **exactly two effective administrators**, both approved for that repository. Declare the complete repository inventory independently of what the API returns, including archived repositories. Repository exclusions are not supported.

Approved users who are not currently owners or administrators do not count toward these limits. Maester collects and reports observed access even when approvals have not been configured; seeing a user in the report does not approve that user.

When member deletion is enabled, Maester checks for policies that may further restrict deletion before confirming an administrator-count or approval failure. An active repository-target policy needs review because Maester cannot verify its effective restrictions or who can bypass it. If no other repository confirms a failure, unresolved policy questions produce **Investigate**. This extra policy review is not needed when the administrator requirements are already met, and it is not part of the owner assessment when member deletion is disabled.

A confirmed failure remains **Failed** even when other information is incomplete. When no failure is confirmed, missing, malformed, or incomplete required GitHub data produces **Skipped**. Otherwise, missing approvals or a repository list that is not confirmed as complete or does not match GitHub require **Investigate**. Invalid configuration, failed requests, and JSON parsing errors produce **Error**, even if earlier observations suggest a failure. The test cannot pass with incomplete information.

Use an organization owner and a token that can read all required settings, users, and repositories. The [approval guide](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/github-deletion-policy) lists the permissions and GHE.com connection requirements and explains how incomplete results are assessed. The check reads only the connected organization and does not attempt deletion or change permissions. Reports contain organization, user, and repository information and should be handled as sensitive assessment data.

#### Remediation action

1. On the connected GitHub web host (`github.com` or your enterprise's `SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com`), open **Your organizations**, select the organization, then go to **Settings** > **Access** > **Member privileges** > **Repository deletion and transfer**.
2. If member deletion is disabled, review **People** filtered to **Owners**. Remove unnecessary assignments, approve the remaining trusted and qualified owners, and keep the number of owners within the configured maximum.
3. If member deletion is enabled, review **Settings** > **Collaborators & teams** for every repository, including access inherited from the organization or enterprise. Ensure exactly two effective administrators are assigned and approve both. Review any restrictive policies identified in the result.
4. Update the approval configuration after access changes. If member deletion is enabled, also update the complete repository inventory. Then run the test again. Changing the member-deletion setting alone does not complete the assessment.

#### Related links

* [CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 - Section 1.2.3](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/github)
* [GitHub: Repository deletion permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/organizations/managing-organization-settings/setting-permissions-for-deleting-or-transferring-repositories)
* [GitHub deletion approval configuration](https://maester.dev/docs/configuration/github-deletion-policy)
* [REST: Organization members](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/orgs/members#list-organization-members)
* [REST: Effective repository collaborators](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/collaborators/collaborators#list-repository-collaborators)

=== 1_2_3
## Description

Ensure only a limited number of trusted users can delete repositories.

## Rationale

Restricting the ability to delete repositories protects the organization from intentional and unintentional data loss. This ensures that users cannot delete repositories or cause other potential damage—whether by accident or due to their account being hacked—unless they have the correct privileges.

**Note**: Certain users will not be permitted to delete repositories.

## Audit

Verify that only a limited number of trusted users can delete repositories.

## Remediation

Enforce repository deletion by a few trusted and responsible users only.
=== 1_2_4
## Description

Ensure only trusted and responsible users can delete issues.

## Rationale

Issues are a way to keep track of things happening in repositories, such as setting new milestones or requesting urgent fixes. Deleting an issue is not a benign activity, as it might harm the development workflow or attempt to hide malicious behavior. Because of this, it should be restricted and allowed only by trusted and responsible users.

**Note**: Certain users will not be permitted to delete issues.

## Audit

Verify that only trusted and responsible users can delete issues.

## Remediation

Restrict issue deletion to a few trusted and responsible users only.

CIS Benchmark: CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0

Assessment Status: Manual

#### Rationale

Deleting repositories can cause major source loss, break delivery workflows, and hide malicious or accidental activity. Repository deletion should therefore be limited to a small set of trusted people whose access is reviewed intentionally.

#### Impact

Members without the required repository or organization role will not be able to delete or transfer repositories. Teams may need a documented owner-led process for repository retirement.

content.text:
CIS asks for less than #2525 enforces. CIS asks you to name trusted people. It never gives a number, and the number limits in the PR are Maester's own.

**What CIS says.** Both items are Manual in CIS GitHub v1.2.0:
- **1.2.3, repository deletion:** "Verify that only a limited number of trusted users can delete repositories." The fix is to allow deletion by "a few trusted and responsible users only."
- **1.2.4, issue deletion:** only "trusted and responsible users" can delete issues.

Neither item says how many owners or admins that should be. My source is the copy of the benchmark text in the Steampipe GitHub compliance mod. The CIS PDF itself needs a login, so I didn't read it. I can't rule out a "two administrators" line in its audit steps.

**What other scanners do:**
- **chain-bench (Aqua)** fails only when the organisation lets members delete repositories (or issues). It doesn't look at who has the access.
- **Steampipe (Turbot)** fails a repository when any of its admins is missing from a trusted-users list you supply. It has no count limit.

**How #2525 compares:**
- **Approved owners and admins list:** this matches what CIS asks, and it's what Steampipe does.
- **At most 3 owners (you can set 1 to 3):** the author made this number up. They say so in the PR, as their reading of CIS's "few".
- **Exactly 2 admins per repository:** this isn't in any public copy of the CIS text. It's the strictest part of the PR and the reason most organisations would fail out of the box.

That backs up the blocking points already in the draft: keep the checks at Investigate until approvals are set up, and question the hard limits. The draft comment still asks the author where "exactly two" comes from.

**Desk:** I've added this comparison as the first finding on the #2525 card and updated it to the new head, 06691925fa53. The author pushed two docs-only commits since the last review, and CI is green: 20 checks passed and 2 were skipped.

######## 2525
Thanks @thetechgy. The evidence handling here is careful: partial lists can only prove a failure, missing data ends up as Skipped or Investigate and never as a pass, and the deletion guide is thorough.

Before we can merge, a few things need a change or a decision.

- **Blocking: out-of-the-box result for CIS.GH.1.2.3 and 1.2.4.** On main these always return Investigate. With this PR and no config, many orgs will fail:
  - Org owners are effective admins on every repository. With member deletion enabled (GitHub's default), any org with three or more owners fails every repository.
  - An org with more than three owners fails the owner check.

  Without `GitHubDeletionPolicy` the checks can never pass. I'd like them to stay Investigate until approvals are configured, and fail only once the config exists.
- **Blocking: API cost.** With member deletion enabled, the check lists collaborators for every repository even when no config exists and a pass is impossible. On a large org that's thousands of calls on every run. Please stop after the inventory read with Investigate when the policy, or its `Repositories` list, is missing.
- **Blocking: please split the PR.** It changes much more than the GitHub CIS checks:
  - the export and redaction pipeline every suite uses (`Invoke-Maester`, `Get-MtHtmlReport`, `ConvertTo-MtRedactedResult`);
  - a new public parameter, `Add-MtTestResultDetail -RedactedResult`;
  - the shared GitHub transport (rate-limit guard, timeouts, metadata and GraphQL helpers).

  Each of these needs its own review. A suggested split:
  1. the 1.2.2, 1.3.2 and 1.3.8 type fixes, which could merge quickly;
  2. GitHub transport and rate limiting;
  3. redacted results;
  4. the deletion checks and `GitHubDeletionPolicy`.
- **Question: "exactly two administrators" and the 1-3 owner cap.** Is "exactly two" the benchmark's audit wording? If not, please make it configurable or soften it. Capping `MaximumOrganizationOwners` at 3 also means an org whose policy allows more owners can't configure that.
- **For the redacted-results PR:**
  - `TestResultRedacted` is still written to JSON and HTML when redaction is off. Please leave it out of those.
  - For imported results, please fall back to the generic redaction rather than throwing on an invalid value.

+function Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember {
+    <#
+    .SYNOPSIS
+    Returns the principals that hold directory roles, with the members of role-assigned groups expanded.
+
+    .DESCRIPTION
+    Reads the role assignments with Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment and returns each assigned principal. When a role
+    is assigned to a group, the group's members are returned instead of the group. Role-assignable groups cannot be
+    nested, so one level is read.
+
+    Unlike Get-MtRoleMember, this throws when a group's members cannot be read, so a check cannot pass without
+    evaluating them. A group that no longer exists (404) is skipped.
+
+    .EXAMPLE
+    Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' -MemberStatus Active
+
+    Returns the principals with an active Global Administrator assignment, including members of role-assigned groups.
+    #>
+    [CmdletBinding()]
+    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
+    param(
+        # The IDs of the role definitions to return members for.
+        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
+        [guid[]]$RoleId,
+
+        # The type of assignments to read. Default is both Eligible and Active.
+        [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active', 'EligibleAndActive')]
+        [string]$MemberStatus = 'EligibleAndActive'
+    )
+
+    $roleAssignments = @((Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId $RoleId -MemberStatus $MemberStatus -ExpandPrincipal -DisableCache).Assignments)
+    foreach ($roleAssignment in $roleAssignments) {
+        $principal = $roleAssignment.principal
+        if ($null -eq $principal) { continue }
+        if ($principal.'@odata.type' -ne '#microsoft.graph.group') {
+            $principal
+            continue
+        }
+
+        try {
+            $groupMembers = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "groups/$($principal.id)/members" -ApiVersion v1.0)
+        } catch {
+            if ($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode -eq 'NotFound') {
+                Write-Verbose "Role-assigned group $($principal.id) was not found and is skipped."
+                continue
+            }
+            throw "Could not read the members of role-assigned group $($principal.id): $($_.Exception.Message)"
+        }
+        foreach ($groupMember in $groupMembers) {
+            if ($null -ne $groupMember) { $groupMember }
+        }
+    }
+}

result.output:
powershell/public/services/entra/Get-MtRoleMember.ps1
function Get-MtRoleMember {
    <#
    .Synopsis
    Returns all the members of a role.

    .Description
    The role can be either active or eligible, defaults to getting members that are both active and eligible.

    If the assigned member is a group, all members of that group will be returned.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator

    Returns all the Global Administrators and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator -MemberStatus Active

    Returns all the Global Administrators that are currently active and excludes those that are eligible but not yet active.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtRoleMember -Role GlobalAdministrator,PrivilegedRoleAdministrator

    Returns all the Global Administrators and Privileged Role administrators and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -RoleId "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

    Returns all the members of the role with the specified RoleId and includes both Eligible and Active members.

    .Example
    Get-MtRoleMember -RoleId "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" -MemberStatus Active

    Returns all the currently active members of the role with the specified RoleId.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtRoleMember
    #>

    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSReviewUnusedParameter', '', Justification = 'ArgumentCompleter requires the full script block signature, even when only wordToComplete is used.')]
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'RoleName')]
    param(
        # The name of the role to get members for.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'RoleName', Position = 0, Mandatory = $true)]
        [ArgumentCompleter({
                param($commandName, $parameterName, $wordToComplete)
                Initialize-MtRoleDefinition
                $roleNames = @($script:MtRoles.Keys) + @($script:MtRoleAliases.Keys)
                $roleNames |
                Where-Object { $_.StartsWith($wordToComplete, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) } |
                Sort-Object | ForEach-Object {
                    [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'ParameterValue', $_)
                }
            })]
        [ValidateScript({
                Initialize-MtRoleDefinition
                $roleNames = @($script:MtRoles.Keys) + @($script:MtRoleAliases.Keys)
                if ($_ -in $roleNames) { return $true }
                throw "Unknown role '$_'. Use tab-completion to see valid role names."
            })]
        [string[]]$Role,

        # The ID of the role to get members for.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'RoleId', Position = 0, Mandatory = $true)]
        [guid[]]$RoleId,

        # The type of members to look for. Default is both Eligible and Active.
        [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active', 'EligibleAndActive')]
        [string]$MemberStatus
    )

    # Ensure the role lookup tables are built. Guards against the module-load-time
    # assignment of $script:MtRoles not persisting into the Pester test-execution
    # context (the cause of the MT.1020 NullReferenceException). See Get-MtRoleInfo.
    Initialize-MtRoleDefinition

    Write-Verbose "Getting members for RoleId: $RoleId, Role: $Role, MemberStatus: $MemberStatus"
    if (-not $MemberStatus) { $MemberStatus = 'EligibleAndActive' }

    if ($Role) {
        # Resolve role names to GUIDs via MtRoleDefinition.ToString(), then explicitly cast to [guid[]]
        # to avoid relying on implicit coercion from MtRoleDefinition through the typed parameter variable.
        $RoleId = [guid[]]($Role | ForEach-Object { (Get-MtRoleInfo -RoleName $_).ToString() })
    }

    $roleAssignments = (Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId $RoleId -MemberStatus $MemberStatus -ExpandPrincipal -DisableCache).Assignments

    foreach ($directoryRoleId in $RoleId) {
        $assignments = @()
        foreach ($roleAssignment in $roleAssignments | Where-Object { $_.roleDefinitionId -eq "$directoryRoleId" }) {
            $principal = $roleAssignment.principal
            if ($null -eq $principal) { continue }

            $members = @($principal)
            if ($principal.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.group') {
                #5/10/2024 - Entra ID Role Enabled Security Groups do not currently support nesting
                # Get-MtGroupMember returns $null when a group cannot be resolved (e.g., GDAP external groups, deleted groups). Skip null results.
                $groupMembers = Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $principal.id
                if ($null -ne $groupMembers) {
                    $members += $groupMembers
                }
            }

            # Append the type of assignment
            foreach ($member in $members) {
                $member | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'AssignmentType' -Value $roleAssignment.AssignmentType -Force
            }
            $assignments += $members
        }

        $assignments | Sort-Object id -Unique
    }
}

content.text:
The main difference is what happens when a role-assigned group's members can't be read. `Get-MtRoleMember` silently drops those people. The new `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` stops with an error instead.

| | `Get-MtRoleMember` (existing, public) | `Get-MtDirectoryRoleMember` (new in #2601, internal) |
|---|---|---|
| Where the assignments come from | `Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -ExpandPrincipal` | The same call |
| Group expansion | One level, through `Get-MtGroupMember` | One level, a direct `groups/{id}/members` call |
| **If a group can't be read** (403, throttling, any error) | `Get-MtGroupMember` writes a warning and returns `$null`. The group's members are left out and the check goes on | **Throws**, so the check reports Error |
| Deleted or missing group (404) | Skipped | Skipped |
| How it recognises a 404 | Checks five forms: enum, `'NotFound'`, `404`, the exception's `StatusCode`, and a match on the message | Checks only `Response.StatusCode -eq 'NotFound'` |
| Group object in the output | Returns the group and its members | Returns the members only |
| Extras | `-Role` by name, tags each member with `AssignmentType`, removes duplicates per role | None. Callers remove duplicates themselves |

**Why the author added it:** with the existing function, a CIS check like 1.1.1 (cloud-only admins) or 1.1.4 (admin licences) can pass even though the members of an unreadable admin group were never checked. The new helper makes that case an Error.

**A risk to raise with the author:** the narrower 404 check. `Get-MtGroupMember` checks several forms because a GDAP partner group or a deleted group doesn't always report a 404 the same way. If one of those 404s doesn't match the single form the new helper checks, the helper throws. Then 1.1.1, 1.1.3 and 1.1.4 would report Error on every tenant with a GDAP group assigned to a role, which covers most MSP-managed tenants.

The fix is to reuse `Get-MtGroupMember`'s 404 check: move it into a small shared helper, or copy the same conditions. The author could also skip the separate function and give `Get-MtGroupMember` a way to throw on errors other than 404, but that changes a public command.

The #2525 unit tests are still running in the background.

Should I add the 404 point to the #2601 card as a finding, with a line in the draft comment asking the author to reuse that check?

content.text:
CodeRabbit asked for it. The author didn't come up with it on their own.

**What prompted it.** On 30 October, CodeRabbit flagged a Major issue on 1.1.4: "Do not pass when group membership cannot be read." The case it described:
- An admin role is assigned to a group.
- Reading that group fails with an error that isn't a 404.
- `Get-MtGroupMember` shows a warning and returns nothing, so `Get-MtRoleMember` carries on as if the group had no members.
- The check then passes without ever looking at those admins.

The same gap affects 1.1.1 and 1.1.3.

CodeRabbit offered two fixes: fail when the group can't be expanded, or change the shared commands so they pass the error on. The author picked the first, with a new internal helper. In their words, they did that because `Get-MtGroupMember` and `Get-MtRoleMember` "are public commands used by other checks and by custom tests". They also pointed to our earlier review asking them to leave shared commands alone in this PR. That review was ours, about `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`. The unit tests cover a 403, which throws, and a 404, which is skipped.

**Why reading a group could fail with something other than a 404:**
- **No permission (403).** The run's token can read role assignments but not group membership. Examples are a custom app registration without `GroupMember.Read.All` or `Directory.Read.All`, or a delegated user who can't see the group. This is the realistic case. The PR now lists `Directory.Read.All` as required for 1.1.4.
- **A group in a restricted management administrative unit**, or one with hidden membership, which can return 403 even with directory read.
- **Throttling (429) or a temporary Graph error (5xx)** that the shared request helper doesn't retry.

In each of these cases the right result is Error, not Pass. So the change is sound.

**A correction to my last answer.** I overstated the 404 risk. Both helpers go through the same `Invoke-MtGraphRequest`, which raises the status as an enum. PowerShell's `-eq 'NotFound'` matches that enum. So the single check in the new helper should catch a normal 404, and the five-way check in `Get-MtGroupMember` is extra caution. The one case I can't confirm is a GDAP partner group, which lives in the partner's tenant. I don't know whether it reaches this code as a 404, or as an assignment with no principal, which the helper skips anyway. It's worth asking the author to test that, but it isn't a blocker.

**One more open point.** After that commit, CodeRabbit raised another Major issue that is still open. The group-member call uses the session cache, unlike the role-assignment call just before it, which bypasses the cache.
